roadmap.goal: Story #6249: a metrics chart that is behind the selected window says so, and never settles on the wrong one. Frontend only, four slices, each releasable on its own. Slice 01a: every dashboard fetch becomes a TanStack query keyed by the request it sends, so a slow answer for a window already left can never land; no visual change. Slice 01b: the shared widget frame draws loading (old chart at 40 % under a 24 px spinner, body refusing the pointer, View Data disabled, aria-busy) and could-not-load (warning icon and the agreed copy under a title + info header) for every chart the page feeds, the E2E waits are wired in and the walking skeleton runs. Slice 01c: the over-time charts and the two filtered views report their own status through the frame. Slice 02: a dashboard opens with every chart's frame in place, the three overview widgets lose their own spinners, and Estimation vs. Cycle Time and Feature Size keep their presence rule but show could-not-load on their own failure. Done when zero `it.skip` remain in the six DISTILL files (widgetStatus.test.ts, WidgetShell.status.test.tsx, ThroughputRunChartCard.loading.test.tsx, PredictabilityScoreDetailsWidget.loading.test.tsx, OverTimeWidgets.loading.test.tsx, BaseMetricsView.loading.test.tsx) and the E2E walking skeleton is un-skipped. That is about 236 pending cases: DISTILL counted 233, and the every-fetch-key failure table in widgetStatus.test.ts grows from 29 to 32 rows once slice 01a adds throughputPbc, cumulativeStateTimeSelection and cumulativeStateTimeScope to getMetricsFetchKeys(). The 20 pins stay green, except the one slice 01b deletes. `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` are green with zero warnings, and the E2E specs each slice touches pass locally.
roadmap.paradigm_note: The Hypothesis + state-delta unit mandate from nw-roadmap does not apply, and leaving it out is deliberate. This is TypeScript + Vitest + React Testing Library + Playwright. fast-check is not a devDependency, so DISTILL wrote property-shaped specifications as it.each example tables (recorded in feature-delta.md, DISTILL / Reconciliation). The crafter writes no new specifications: every pending Vitest case and the E2E walking skeleton were written by DISTILL and are skipped. RED means un-skipping them and capturing the failure before the production edit; GREEN is the production code. The crafter edits tests only where DISTILL's disposition lists it (QueryClientProvider wrappers, re-pointed callbacks, deleted spinner tests, the one pin slice 01b deletes) and in the E2E POM and spec re-pointing that slice 01b owns. Code comments follow the project rule: plain-language why only, never a pointer such as DDD-5, R8, E2, M1 or AC-1.3. Steps tagged @sizing-review-needed un-skip eight or more cases; each says why in its implementation_notes.

validation.notes: Conditionally approved on re-review (0 blockers). Condition: each step's file-qualified `unskips` list is the authoritative spec-to-step mapping; scenario_name names the main describe only (02-02 and 02-04 span several describes). Entries marked as pins are passing guards, not un-skips; a suffix such as (it.each, 7 rows) is an annotation, not part of the title. 01-04 lists the two filter-off pins as one string: the real titles end "own series for it" (ThroughputRunChartCard) and "own score for it" (PredictabilityScoreDetailsWidget).

user_decisions: S1: on a re-fetch the chart drops to 40 % opacity under a 24 px centred CircularProgress; the header stays at full strength.
S2 / M1: while loading, the whole body box widget-shell-body-<key> takes pointer-events none and no child opts back in; View Data is disabled; the info button still works. No `inert`.
S3 / M4: on failure the chart is removed; WarningAmberIcon and exactly 'This chart couldn't be loaded. Change the dates or reload to try again.'; no Retry.
S4: with nothing to dim, a lone 24 px spinner at the widget's normal height under a title + info header.
M2: a could-not-load frame shows title + info only: no rating chip, trend or View Data.
M3: Estimation vs. Cycle Time and Feature Size keep today's presence rule but show could-not-load, with no spinner, when their own fetch fails, on first load or later.
O1 accepted: no client timeout; a request that never answers keeps its widget loading.
O4 accepted: TanStack Query (already installed, MIT) for the useMetricsData fetches and the two filtered views; the over-time hooks are NOT moved (E5).
out_of_scope: Forecast and backtest Run-button spinners, the Overview page, Feature and Delivery pages, every page-level LoadingAnimation.
Moving usePbcOverTime / usePercentilesOverTime to TanStack Query (E5): they keep their cancelled cleanup and per-mount cache and only return a status.
Any backend, API, RBAC, client or usage-data change (DEVOPS answered usage data N/A).
A retry button, a client timeout, caching across windows.
The named-percentiles scope fetch: its generation counter stays, and its failure still reverts to the Default percentiles (R3).
Mutation testing, refactor passes, review and finalize: the orchestrator runs those after every step below.

phases.name: Slice 01a: a chart never settles on the wrong window
phases.description: Every useMetricsData fetch, the two filtered views and the Cumulative Time per State paths become queries keyed by the request they send. An answer for a window already left lands in its own cache entry and is never read. Nothing looks different yet: a failure still leaves the last good value on screen, as today. Releasable alone: it removes the 'old window lands last and stays' defect and the three stale-window bugs that already existed.

With several queries for one key: any failed query makes the key error. Otherwise any query on its way, or still showing the previous window, makes it loading. Otherwise it is ready. A failure beside a query still on its way reads error.
hasData is true when the key shows some window's answer, including the previous window's placeholder. It is false for a request on its way for the first time.

steps.implementation_notes: Pure function, return-only contract. Placeholder data counts as loading: keepPreviousData shows the previous key's answer while the current key has none, and that is what the dimmed old chart is made of later. This is the first GREEN that implements widgetStatus.ts, so it removes the `__SCAFFOLD__` export and the comment that calls the file a RED scaffold. useMetricsData exports one shared metricsQueryOptions object (staleTime 0, gcTime 0, retry false, refetchOnWindowFocus false). Every query this step creates spreads it, and the app-wide QueryClient defaults are never changed.
One query per service call: the cycle-time batch becomes five queries, and the previous-period Work Item Age percentiles call belongs to the workItemAgePercentiles key.
Query keys carry the fetch name, the owner type and id, the dates as formatLocalDate local-day strings, and every choice the call sends. The query function reads its arguments from that key.
Every query function returns null where the service answered undefined.
These queries use placeholderData keepPreviousData. The hook keeps its value-shaped return, so BaseMetricsView reads the same names, and it adds fetchStates per fetch key, built with fetchKeyStateOf.

steps.implementation_notes: Scope of this step: every fetch key that getFetchKeysForCategories(['flow-metrics'], owner) returns, for both owners, with throughput first. The remaining keys move in 01-03 and stay effects until then; both paths coexist safely. The key is the race guard. A late answer for a window already left lands under that window's key and is never read, so no cancelled flag or AbortController is added (no service takes a signal). Dates go into keys as formatLocalDate strings, the way usePbcOverTime's cacheKey already does, so two Date objects for the same day never make two requests. Undefined becomes null because a nullish answer must read as answered-with-nothing, never as still-waiting. The last-success fallback is a per-metric reference reset on owner change. It is temporary: 02-04 retires it once the frame can say a chart could not be loaded. The added unit test is the one DISTILL left for DELIVER (feature-delta.md, Existing-test disposition). The shared options object is created here, but its read-back test, the 8-row it.each 'on a %s's %s is asked for without retrying, and kept for no other window', is un-skipped in 01-03. That test is one table spanning every category, Vitest cannot un-skip some of its rows, and it can only pass once every dashboard fetch is a query. Rendering-heavy test files may hit Vitest's 5000 ms default: give the slow test an explicit timeout instead of treating it as a flake (docs/ci-learnings.md). Commit: `feat(metrics): flow metrics fetches answer the window they were asked for (story 6249)`

criteria: Every pending case in the five describes 'a widget's status, from the things it waits on', 'which widgets are behind the selected window', 'Cumulative Time per State narrowed by the reader', 'every request a chart waits on' and 'whether a chart has an older picture to dim' is un-skipped, and is RED (scaffold error) before the edit.
combineWidgetStatuses: any error gives error; otherwise any loading gives loading; otherwise ready. An empty list is ready, and order never changes the answer.

widgetStatusFor(widgetKey, keyStates, isCommitPending): its inputs are the fetch keys that getFetchRequirementsForWidget lists. While a step is pending, the page's own keys read loading whatever their state, including a key that failed. A widget with no page keys (Percentiles / PBC Over Time) reads loading while a step is pending and ready otherwise. Once the window is committed, one failed input makes the widget error at once, without waiting for siblings still in flight.

A missing entry or an inapplicable key never holds a widget back. A failure in a key a widget does not show leaves it ready. Every fetch key that can fail ends exactly the placed widgets that require it in error.
widgetHasData is true only when every key the widget shows has answered some window.
After this step, zero `it.skip` remain in widgetStatus.test.ts except 'reports nothing, and breaks nothing, when it is drawn outside a dashboard frame' (03-01).
`pnpm test` green; `pnpm build` green with zero warnings.
steps.implementation_notes: Pure functions, return-only. This module is the prime mutation target, so keep the precedence in one place. The pending flag rewrites only the page's keys and never a self-fetching child's report. A page key's failure is for a window the reader is leaving, while a child's own failure is real (the child side arrives in 03-01). Sizing: this step un-skips about 91 cases, far above the eight-case guide. Four it.each tables generate most of them: 35 placed widgets, one row per fetch key, 7 precedence rows and 6 Cumulative Time per State rows. The fetch-key table counted 29 rows at DISTILL and grows to 32 because 01a added throughputPbc, cumulativeStateTimeSelection and cumulativeStateTimeScope to getMetricsFetchKeys(). The declared tests number thirteen, over three small pure functions. Splitting them across steps would leave later steps un-skipping cases that are already green, which fakes their RED. Commit: `feat(metrics): one rule decides whether a chart is ready, loading or failed (story 6249)`

steps.implementation_notes: The maintainer's decisions, in plain words. The old chart stays visible but faded to 40 %, with a small 24 px spinner over it, and the header stays at full strength. View Data is disabled because it would list the old window's items. The whole body (chart and in-chart controls) ignores the pointer while loading, by pointer-events none on the one body box, and the info button keeps working. Do not use inert: it would also hide the dimmed chart from assistive technology, where aria-busy is the signal. Keep the status branches in a small sub-component so WidgetShell's render body stays under Sonar's cognitive-complexity limit. The self-fetching child must stay mounted under the spinner (out of sight is enough) so that its later report is not lost. Sizing: ten cases, two over the guide. steps.implementation_notes: One presence rule at the one wrap site, instead of a 'render a spinner when null' branch in 25 nodes. An item is kept when its node exists or its status is not ready, and its children stay null until every fetch key it needs has had data at least once. Presence comes from the category's placement, so nothing pops in and the layout never reshuffles. The overview widgets take non-null props, and their nodes are built `x ? <Widget/> : null` like every other node. Their own spinners must go in the same commit as the frames: the first-load table asserts exactly one progressbar per frame, so a frame plus the widget's own spinner fails it, and a widget whose node is null cannot be framed. Estimation vs. Cycle Time stays hidden while estimation is not set up, and Feature Size while the window holds no Features: today's rule, kept by maintainer decision. Their failure case is 04-02. Sizing: 22 cases, well over the guide. Every one turns on the same wrap-site change, and the spinner coupling above keeps them in one commit.
